findings.finding: The recovery loops require every 32-request batch to be uniformly 503 unless every response is 200. Neither CONFIG-D10, CONFIG-P5, CONFIG-003 nor the implementation record defines a client burst as one atomic readiness snapshot. Each request samples the monotonic retry cutoff independently. Requests arriving just before the cutoff can return cached false, while requests arriving at or after it join one successful initialization and return true. Promise.all joins client promises; it does not give the HTTP server a batch transaction or identical request arrival times. The listener-free loop contains the same unsupported assertion, though its 275ms delay reduces exposure.
findings.reproduction: Execute the actual emitted refreshPersistenceReadiness algorithm with a controlled clock and successful initialization stub. Begin unready with persistenceNextAttemptAt=250. Call 16 requests at t=249 and 16 at t=250 before awaiting the combined promises. Observed 16 false and 16 true, exactly one initialization and one client replacement. Separately 32 calls during one pending eligible initialization all join it and become true.
findings.requiredCorrection: Validate each response's status and corresponding safe body independently, accepting 200/ready/available and 503/not_ready/unavailable during the transition. Retain bounded eventual all-ready observation, one user-schema initialization, authenticated route success and secret checks. Add a deterministic retry-cutoff interleaving regression rather than imposing artificial server-wide batch uniformity. Do not weaken the one-in-flight requirement.

findings.finding: A recoverable SQLite schema-initialization lock is classified as a fatal incompatible-schema/startup failure. isPersistenceAvailabilityFailure excludes SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED, and initializePersistenceOnce sends every other error into persistenceInitializationFatal=true. refreshPersistenceReadiness then returns false forever without retry; the generated main exits before listening. The failure is contention, not invalid configuration or incompatible schema, so this can create a restart loop and violates recovery without restart for transient required-storage unavailability.
findings.reproduction: Create a disposable SQLite database, hold BEGIN EXCLUSIVE from a separate connection, and load the existing generated persistence-seed target. Instrument Database.prototype.exec only in the probe to capture structured codes: CREATE TABLE raises SQLITE_BUSY, errno=5. Release the lock with ROLLBACK and call refreshPersistenceReadiness: false, fatal flag remains true. A separate generated-main subprocess under the same lock exits 1 with RUNTIME_STARTUP_FAILED and no runtime.live/runtime.ready log. No product source was modified.
findings.requiredCorrection: Classify listed transient initialization contention separately from fatal schema/configuration faults and allow bounded single-flight retry after the lock clears. Preserve genuinely incompatible internal-schema failures as fatal and keep configuration validation before listener binding. Add a real initial-lock and recovery-time-lock regression, without changing ordinary statement contention into whole-database unavailability or expanding transaction replay semantics.

reviewedWithoutNewFinding: Eligible asynchronous recovery has one in-flight promise; a pending 32-call probe initialized once and replaced the client once after settlement. Backoff caps at five seconds and success resets delay to 250ms with a one-second healthy cache.

The HTTP handler answers /health/live before awaiting readiness or consulting the required-database traffic gate. Live SQLite tests keep the process alive through missing-path startup and recover without restart. This does not prove liveness under synchronous event-loop blocking or hung initial imports.

Ordinary routes receive dependency_unavailable/503 while the database flag is false; recovered protected identity succeeds. Auth-storage recovery reaches initializeAuthenticationStorage before readiness success, and the harness provisions/uses a session only after observing recovery. The harness is test-only, loopback-bound and not a generated production endpoint.

Readiness bodies derive HTTP status, status and database state from the same per-request boolean. Fixed database ID and compiler-derived quoted snake-case service IDs prevent endpoint/credential/native-error details entering the normal health response.

Advisory services are deduplicated by a BTreeSet of compiler-derived IDs and rendered as unprobed. No provider function is called by readiness and advisory output does not influence the ready boolean. Focused instrumentation confirms zero connect/fetch calls for reminder_mail.

Invalid typed startup configuration is checked before listener creation. Fatal incompatible authentication schemas remain blocked before listener binding, with fresh focused evidence. Normal health/error output and debug-disabled startup checks retain canary redaction. Debug-stack-enabled diagnostics are not approved by these tests.
openAcceptanceAndLimits: Hard active-call readiness deadlines remain unapproved: target.rs:5852 awaits the PostgreSQL query after requesting cancel at one second. The user reports query.cancel did not interrupt an application query on Bun 1.2.20. A cancel hook alone cannot establish a bounded readiness response.

Initialization bounds remain open: application/auth schema calls have no whole-initialization deadline; top-level await initializePersistenceOnce occurs before listener setup. connectionTimeout=2 only constrains its connection boundary, not all schema work or authentication setup. A blocked initial import can prevent even /health/live from becoming reachable.

Single-flight bounds active dependency attempts, not the number of HTTP requests waiting on a stalled attempt. SQLite probes and schema operations are synchronous, so timer-based hard interruption and event-loop liveness are not established.

No independent PostgreSQL startup/outage/auth-recovery test was run, and the pinned supported gate stopped before its later PostgreSQL steps. Prior passing reports cannot approve current-source hard bounds. Transaction timeout enforcement is excluded from this review and does not establish readiness timeout enforcement.

The reviewed direct-handler auth outage case renames/restores the session table; it proves safe route rejection and recovery, not deployment readiness becoming false for every schema-level auth outage. The deployment health probe checks database connectivity/schema_version rather than all auth tables on every request.
